quote.translation: For Lotze the ways of arriving at necessary knowledge are limited to these three, and there is no other (Lotze, Logik, hrsg. v. Misch, Leipzig, 1912, S. 65).

regions.text: ヘーゲルも必然性を具現する絶對的開係としてご實性と屬性との關係三因果性の開係三交互作用の開係の三つを最げてある。

quote.translation: Hegel likewise names three absolute relations in which necessity is realised: (1) the relation of substantiality and accident, (2) the relation of causality and (3) the relation of reciprocal action.

regions.text: さうして實體が必然性の機念を充實するためには實體が原因として、屬性が結果として把握されなければならぬすずなはち實鱧屬性の開係が因果開係へ移り行かなければなら双としてゐる。

quote.translation: For substance to fulfil the concept of necessity it must be grasped as cause and its accident as effect, which means that the relation of substance and accident must pass over into the causal relation.

regions.text: また因果系列が異に無限であるためには因果系列は直線の形を取らずに圓形を取らねばならぬずなはち因果性は交互作用に

quote.translation: And for the causal series to be truly infinite it must leave the straight line and take the form of a circle, so that causality becomes reciprocal action.

quote.translation: In this way Hegel sets out the inner connection among the three kinds of necessity (Hegel, Encyklopädie, hrsg. v. Bolland, 1906, §§ 150-156).

quote.translation: Let us call these three modes of necessity (1) categorical necessity, (2) hypothetical necessity and (3) disjunctive necessity.

quote.translation: Distinctions in the relation of judgements are usually named with the standard logical terms teigenteki (定言的), kagenteki (假言的) and sengenteki (選言的), but we deliberately use teigenteki, kasetsuteki (假說的) and risetsuteki (離接的).
